#!/bin/bash
# Live-session watcher v2: emits ONLY notable events (orders, lifecycle, settlement, halts, errors, service-down).
STATE=/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-spson-Projects-Claude-bolt-v2/1786daad-2813-4e03-8c4e-1ce8aa1d66ba/scratchpad/watch2.state
: > "$STATE"
tick=0
REMOTE='{"commands":["systemctl is-active bolt-v2 || echo SERVICE-DOWN","EV=/srv/bolt-v2/var/bolt-v3-live/catalog/bolt-v3/decision-evidence/order-intents.jsonl","echo === NOTABLE ===","tail -n 4000 $EV 2>/dev/null | grep -E \"\\\"kind\\\":\\\"(order_intent|order_lifecycle|settlement|settlement_booking_error|forced_flat|exit_decision|loss_governor_halt|capital_admission_rebuild_audit|order_reject)\" | tail -8 || true","echo === JOURNAL ===","journalctl -u bolt-v2 --since \"110 seconds ago\" --no-pager 2>/dev/null | grep -Ei \"ERROR|panic|halt|kill.?switch|flatten|diverg|Degraded|filled|rejected|denied|submitted\" | tail -5 || true","echo === DISK ===","df --output=pcent /srv | tail -1"]}'
while true; do
  tick=$((tick+1))
  CID=$(aws ssm send-command --region eu-west-2 --instance-ids i-0d544aeb04c3824e4 \
    --document-name AWS-RunShellScript --timeout-seconds 60 \
    --parameters "$REMOTE" --query 'Command.CommandId' --output text 2>/dev/null) \
    || { sleep 90; continue; }
  sleep 12
  OUT=$(aws ssm get-command-invocation --region eu-west-2 --command-id "$CID" --instance-id i-0d544aeb04c3824e4 --query 'StandardOutputContent' --output text 2>/dev/null) || { sleep 80; continue; }
  if echo "$OUT" | head -1 | grep -qE "SERVICE-DOWN|inactive|failed"; then
    echo "ALERT: bolt-v2 service is not active"
  fi
  NOTABLE=$(echo "$OUT" | sed -n '/=== NOTABLE ===/,/=== JOURNAL ===/p' | grep -v '===' | head -8)
  if [ -n "$NOTABLE" ]; then
    while IFS= read -r line; do
      h=$(echo "$line" | shasum | cut -c1-16)
      if ! grep -q "$h" "$STATE" 2>/dev/null; then
        echo "$h" >> "$STATE"
        echo "$line" | python3 -c 'import sys,json
for l in sys.stdin:
    try:
        d=json.loads(l)
        keys=[k for k in ("kind","market_id","instrument_id","transition","outcome","side","quantity","price","reason","settlement_key","realized_pnl") if d.get(k)]
        print("EVENT:", {k:d[k] for k in keys})
    except Exception:
        print("EVENT:", l[:300])'
      fi
    done <<< "$NOTABLE"
  fi
  JLINES=$(echo "$OUT" | sed -n '/=== JOURNAL ===/,/=== DISK ===/p' | grep -v '===' | head -5)
  [ -n "$JLINES" ] && echo "$JLINES"
  if [ $((tick % 10)) -eq 0 ]; then
    pc=$(echo "$OUT" | tail -1 | tr -d ' ')
    echo "heartbeat tick=$tick: service active, disk=$pc"
  fi
  sleep 78
done

**The exit fired — 680 times. It couldn't land because there is no one to sell to: the order book on your side of the market is genuinely empty.**

Here's the full picture, verified from the machine's own records:

- **The strategy is not asleep.** It's been re-evaluating the exit at full tick speed and has submitted 680 exit attempts, every one recorded. All 680 died with the identical reason: *"Empty order book: no liquidity available for market order."* It was willing to dump at one cent — there were no bids at any price.
- **The book feed is healthy** — I checked: book updates for this exact token are still streaming in, the connection has zero errors. The updates simply say the bid side is empty. That's the real market: you hold UP tokens, BTC is ~$124 below the interval's open, and nobody buys the losing side of a binary near expiry. A "stop loss" cannot execute against an empty book — that's physics, not a malfunction.
- **Critically, all 680 rejects were local** — the system computed there was nothing to cross and refused *before* sending anything. The venue never saw a single one. Compare July 2: in this exact situation the old system fabricated 40 phantom sells and *believed* it had exited. The new one refuses to lie, keeps the position honestly managed, and records every attempt.

**What happens next:** the position rides to resolution — which is exactly the settlement test this session wanted. If BTC stays below the open, the UP tokens settle at zero and the loss is the entry cost (bounded by the $10-per-order cap — the deposit's still ~$41+ regardless). If BTC recovers before the interval ends, they settle at $1 each. Either way, **settlement booking — the last unproven piece of the money loop — will fire for real**, and my watch will report the settlement records the moment they land.

**The genuine lesson for the record** (this goes in signal grading, not a bug list): on binaries, exit liquidity evaporates precisely when you most want out. If the strategy wants a real stop-loss, it has to exit *earlier*, while losing-side bids still exist — that's a threshold/timing question for the graded-data pass, not a code defect. Nothing to do right now — we watch resolution and settlement.

Your direct observation of the market is evidence against it, and there's a known seam (the strategy manages book subscriptions per state) where a local book can go empty while the venue's is fine. The timing distribution decides this: if the 680 attempts all cluster in the final seconds, empty-at-the-end is plausible; if they span minutes while you saw bids on screen, we have a local book bug.
